issues.description: Constructor Bookstore.init: The problem statement requires an initializer with signature init(books: [Book]) (problem_statement.md lines 9-12). The solution implementation declares init(books: [Book], valid: Bool) in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift (line 14). The solution's Client calls Bookstore(books: books) in Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift (line 57). This mismatch between the declared constructor and both the problem specification and the call site will cause a compilation error and prevents a student from running the provided solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore initializer signature consistent. Preferred fix: change the initializer in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift to init(books: [Book]) (remove the extra 'valid: Bool' parameter) so it matches the problem statement and the Client call. Ensure all call sites use the single-parameter initializer. Alternatively, if an extra parameter is intentional, update the problem statement and all call sites (e.g. Client) to document and use the two-parameter initializer consistently.

issues.description: Constructor mismatch for the Bookstore concept: the problem statement requires an initializer with the signature init(books: [Book]) (problem_statement.md lines 9-12). The solution implementation declares init(books: [Book], valid: Bool) (solution_repository/Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift lines 14-16), while the solution's Client constructs a Bookstore with Bookstore(books: books) (solution_repository/Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift line 57). This introduces an unexpected parameter name ('valid') and an extra constructor parameter that does not appear in the problem statement or the client call, which will confuse students and can produce a compilation/API mismatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore initializer match the problem statement and client usage: change the solution signature to init(books: [Book]) (remove the extra 'valid' parameter). Alternatively, if an extra parameter is intentionally required, give it a default value (e.g. valid: Bool = true) and document it so the signature remains compatible with the expected init(books:) usage and existing Client code.
